applicabilityConditions.analysis: temporal averaging: 2 frames for tactile trials, 8 frames for injection trials, to reduce noise; motion correction by SIFT-based registration; brain masking by flood fill (scikit-image flood); bleach correction: subtract the bottom 5% of pixels within the brain from each frame; baseline autofluorescence subtraction
applicabilityConditions.anesthesia: 3-4% isoflurane for induction; maintained at 1.25-1.5% during imaging (from trial file names); depth confirmed by loss of righting reflex, ~1 breath per second, no toe-pinch response
applicabilityConditions.imaging: 10 frames per second, 13.4 x 11.3 mm, 5 um/px with no binning; cropped to the brain and binned 4 x 4 for all trials
applicabilityConditions.invasiveness: through-skull, label-free; no craniotomy, no transgenic animals, no dye or virus injection
applicabilityConditions.preparation: head-fixed with earbars in a stereotaxic frame (Kopf); heating pad; hair removed with Nair; eye ointment; 1 mL body-temperature sterile saline subcutaneous; 0.1 mL 1% lidocaine subcutaneous under the scalp; scalp removed; periosteum cleaned; thin layer of cyanoacrylate glue applied to the skull for optical clarity
applicabilityConditions.readout: flavoprotein autofluorescence, dF/F over a region of interest
applicabilityConditions.statistics: none reported; no significance testing, no power analysis, no detection limit stated anywhere in the pub

confidence.basis: three trials, consistent with known anatomy and with published flavoprotein imaging, but each n = 1 and obtained after per-trial tuning

cost.note: 13 imaging trials across 5 mice. The pub reports the imaging system cost (approximately US$30,000 including the camera) as capital, not as the cost of this study; no per-study cost is given.

complianceIds: All animal work performed in accordance with the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee of the Charles River Accelerator and Development Lab (CRADL, South San Francisco, CA). No protocol number is given in the pub.

outcomeSummary: Contralateral, somatotopically appropriate responses for right hindlimb, left hindlimb and right forelimb stimulation; a 1-3% increase in autofluorescence above baseline after averaging 50 stimulations.
provenanceNotes: The troubleshooting loop in this stage means the tactile signal was tuned into existence per session. This does not undermine the positive result, but it is why the tactile response is recorded as an internal positive control for later trials rather than as an independent one.
question: Can the ultra-widefield microscope reproduce known somatotopic cortical responses to tactile stimulation, and thereby qualify a session for chemical stimuli?

Raw and processed autofluorescence neuroimaging data

conditions.anesthesia: 3-4% isoflurane for induction; maintained at 1.25-1.5% during imaging (from trial file names); depth confirmed by loss of righting reflex, ~1 breath per second, no toe-pinch response
conditions.expectation: brain activity in S1 (primary somatosensory area), based on refs 19-20
conditions.stimulator: vibrating motor (Amazon B07Q1ZV4MJ) taped to the paw, driven by a simple circuit on two AA batteries

stages.label: vibrating tactile stimulation of a single limb
stages.note: If we didn't detect a cortical response in S1, we performed the following troubleshooting steps and tried again ... In most cases, one or more of these steps resulted in a clear signal. Once we observed a brain response to a tactile stimulus, we proceeded with chemical stimuli. A trial was therefore repeated with adjusted settings until a signal appeared, which means the tactile result is a tuned positive rather than a first-pass one.
stages.protocol: 50 vibrational pulses, 2 s on, 4 s off, imaged simultaneously at 10 fps
protocolAdaptations: adjusted the positioning of the stimulator
reduced the isoflurane level by 0.25% (never below 1%)
placed the stimulator on a different limb

stages.label: imaging analysis pipeline
stages.method: temporal averaging: 2 frames for tactile trials, 8 frames for injection trials, to reduce noise; motion correction by SIFT-based registration; brain masking by flood fill (scikit-image flood); bleach correction: subtract the bottom 5% of pixels within the brain from each frame; baseline autofluorescence subtraction
stages.note: for visualisation, pixel intensities in vehicle and drug trials were scaled to a shared min and max; dF/F was computed on non-adjusted baseline-subtracted data

successCriteria: A localized autofluorescence increase in the somatosensory area contralateral to the stimulated limb, at the anatomically expected position.
title: Vibrotactile stimulation produces localized contralateral somatosensory autofluorescence (assay validation)
